If you're struggling on normal, try it on easy. The combat in the game is tactical so it can be difficult to get into.

First and foremost I'd suggest you make sure the companion is using defensive abilities if you have him set up as a tank. He should have shield defense or shield wall activated. Be sure to pick up defensive skills for him rather than offensive ones to start off. You'll also want to give him a decent amount of dex rather than focusing on constitution, it allows him to avoid attacks. The second priority should be mental resistance. Since the companion is a templar he can pretty easily become nearly immune to magic spells as well.

Make sure you've got your party tactics set up so they'll take health potions when their health is low, and you should stock up on potions so you can throw out heals in a pinch.

Combine that with using taunt efficiently and making sure the companion is in the enemy's line of sight first will make sure that the rest of your party isn't taking damage and you only have one target to heal. There's no reason for you to spend all your mana by starting out with big spells unless you're wading through the deep roads. You doing that also ensures the enemies will gang up on you rather than the tank.

As for yourself, pick up mana clash so you can neutralize enemy casters. It's the cheesiest spell in the game. If you're struggling with how to tackle the combat, try watching some videos on youtube to see what seasoned players are doing. The game really isn't unreasonably hard, it just requires a different approach than action-oriented combat.

Also mages are ridiculously overpowered in the base game so swap one of the dps out for a specific character to start with.

You just need to direct the class to disarm traps, they won't do it automatically. If you're in a trap-heavy area, stop your party and control the class to take out the traps.

Cleansing Aura from the spirit healer tree will heal injuries, but otherwise turn around and go buy more. Don't go into a fight with injured party members, it's a vicious cycle that will end up with you dying more and more. 

Make sure one of your party members has herbalism and they'll be able to craft injury kits for you. Having poison making on another follower so they can craft bombs and poisons should also help you out if you're struggling. Make sure you give your melee at least one skill in poison so they can coat their weapons.

If you have several followers running away from enemies it sounds like you need to utilize the tank better. While it's possible to play origins without a tank the game is easiest with a classic party setup. When the enemy are focusing on a tank the rest of your party won't take as much damage. If you're using a certain companion make sure he has defensive skills like Shield Defense or Shield Wall, and that he's using Taunt and not just Threaten. Have him run in first since the enemies engage the first character they see. Make sure you give him some dex after you've met your strength requirements so can evade attacks. 

Also kiting is the best strategy against ogres and other mini-bosses if you don't have CC skills yet. Just keep an eye on who the orge is chasing, switch to that character to run around, and let the others do ranged damage.

I would also suggest going down to easy difficult while you're getting used to the combat in origins. Anything above easy requires you to pause in combat and control your party members so you can make sure everyone is using the right abilities as efficiently as possible, and that's easier once you have a better grasp of how the other classes and their skills work.

Lastly, make sure someone picks up herbalism so you can make your own potions and injury kits, and don't be afraid to let your party use them when they need to.
